draft.title: Using resources sustainably
card: Resources such as water, soil, forests and fish can run low if they are used faster than they are replaced.
meeting the needs and wants of people today without leaving too little for people in the future.
Sustainable choices include taking only as many fish as the population can replace, or planting new trees after cutting some down.
Using a resource faster than it is replaced is not sustainable. Future generations may then have less of it to meet their own needs and wants.
draft.remember: Sustainable use looks after today's needs and wants and leaves enough for the future.

a.q: Which choice is an example of using a resource sustainably?
opts: A town limits water use so supplies last through dry years
A town uses as much water as it can while dams are full
A town sells its water to other places for quick profit
A town uses water freely and hopes for rain later
a.why: Limiting water use means people today can meet their needs and enough is left for the future. Using as much as possible while dams are full is tempting, but it ignores what will be left later.
a.clue: Which choice thinks about people in the future?

b.q: Ben's fishing business in Tasmania catches only as many fish each year as the population can replace. Why is this sustainable?
opts: It meets needs today and leaves fish for the future
It means the business catches no fish at all
It means people today go without fish to eat
It means the fish are no longer a limited resource
b.why: Catching only what the population can replace means people can use fish now and the fish will still be there later. It is not about going without: sustainable use still meets needs and wants today.
b.clue: Think about both today and the future.

a.best: A town limits water use so supplies last through dry years

b.best: It meets needs today and leaves fish for the future

problems.detail: The distractors are very weak. 'It means the business catches no fish at all' contradicts the stem, which says the business does catch fish. The right option is also the only one that differs in form from the 'It means…' pattern and echoes the remember line, so students can pick it without understanding sustainability.

proposal.title: Using resources sustainably
card: Resources such as water, soil, forests and fish can run low if they are used faster than they are replaced.
meeting the needs and wants of people today without leaving too little for people in the future.
Sustainable choices include taking only as many fish as the population can replace, so enough are left to breed. Planting new trees after cutting some down is another.
Using a resource faster than it is replaced is not sustainable. Future generations may then have less of it to meet their own needs and wants.
proposal.remember: Sustainable use looks after today's needs and wants and leaves enough for the future.

a.q: Which choice is an example of using a resource sustainably?

a.clue: Which choice thinks about people in the future?

b.q: Ben's fishing business in Tasmania catches only as many fish each year as the population can replace. Why is this sustainable?
opts: Enough fish are left to breed for catches in future years
Every customer today can buy as many fish as they want
The business makes a bigger profit from each year's catch
Fish are a resource that can never run low in Tasmania
b.why: Ben leaves enough fish to breed, so people can eat fish now and there will still be fish later. Giving every customer all the fish they want only looks after today, and taking too many would leave too few for the future.
b.clue: Sustainable use looks at more than just this year.
